newsitem.title: UK: UK people have final say on EMU - Labour's Brown.
newsitem.headline: UK people have final say on EMU - Labour's Brown.

text.p: The British electorate not politicians will make the final choice on whether Britain is to join a single European currency, said Gordon Brown, the opposition Labour Party's finance spokesman.

"What hasn't got across to people in this election is that the final decision on this matter, if it's recommended in the next parliament, won't actually be made by the British government," he said in an interview with BBC Radio.
Brown said the government would decide whether to recommend British membership of European monetary union by looking at the convergence criteria and domestic economic interest.
The cabinet would need to recommend joining EMU to parliament, parliament would have to recommend it in a referendum and then the British people would vote on it, Brown said.
Brown said the UK would have to be sure that joining EMU would create more job opportunities and inward investment.
The main sovereignty issues in joining EMU are the right to tax and spend, Brown said.

"There is no decision that I would ever allow that would give up the British veto on these issues so the decisions to tax and spend are of course matters of sovereignty and we would not give these up," he said.
Brown's opposition Labour Party has a comfortable opinion poll lead over the ruling Conservative Party in the run-up to the May 1 election.
